stemBlocks.value: A vendor buys x kg of peanuts and y kg of cashew nuts. (a)(i) She must buy a minimum of 10 kg of peanuts and a minimum of 5 kg of cashew nuts — write two inequalities. (ii) She buys no more than 60 kg of nuts in total; peanuts cost $4.00 per kg, cashews $8.00 per kg, and she spends at least $200 — write two inequalities. (b) Draw the graph of the four inequalities (2 cm to 10 kg on each axis) and shade only the region satisfying all four. (c) The profit is $2.00 per kg of peanuts and $5.00 per kg of cashews: (i) use the graph to find the number of kilograms of each nut for maximum profit, (ii) calculate the maximum profit.
Think first: Two of these constraints are about weight and one is about money — keep the units apart as you write them.

strategyBlocks.value: Write the four inequalities, simplify the cost one, find the corners of the region, then test P = 2x + 5y at each corner.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a)(i) x ≥ 10 and y ≥ 5  (ii) x + y ≤ 60 and 4x + 8y ≥ 200 (i.e. x + 2y ≥ 50)  (b) Region with vertices (10, 20), (10, 50), (55, 5) and (40, 5)  (c)(i) 10 kg of peanuts and 50 kg of cashew nuts  (ii) Maximum profit = 2(10) + 5(50) = $270

whyThisWorks.value: Every constraint is linear, so the set of possible purchases is a polygon and a linear profit function reaches its greatest value at one of its corners. Cashews earn $5 per kg against $2 for peanuts, so profit rises fastest by loading up on cashews; the vendor therefore buys only the compulsory 10 kg of peanuts and fills the remaining allowance of the 60 kg limit with cashews.
